column2: Through giving a man becomes an enjoyer, through serving the aged he becomes wise, and through non-harm he is long-lived, so the wise say.
Therefore he should give and not beg, honour the righteous, speak to himself, do what is dear, be pure, and harm no creature.
Whether authority arises, or nature, or pleasure and pain, among gnats, insects and ants, be steady, Yudhishthira.
[Bhishma] This is the lineage of the gods together with the lineage of sages, recited at both twilights, my son, a supreme remover of sin.
The god, teacher of gods and asuras, saluted by all beings, inconceivable and indescribable, the life of all, unborn of womb;
the Grandsire, lord of the world; Savitri, Brahma's virtuous wife; the Veda; the earth; the Maker; Vishnu, Narayana, the lord;
Uma's lord, Virupaksha, Skanda the general, Vishakha, the Fire, the Wind, the Moon and Sun, the makers of light;
Shakra, lord of Shachi; Yama with Dhumorna; Varuna with Gauri; and the lord of wealth with Riddhi;
the gentle cow, the goddess Surabhi, and the great sage Vishrava; the six Seasons, the Ocean, Ganga's streams, and the hosts of Maruts;
the Valakhilyas perfected by austerity, Krishna Dvaipayana, Narada and Parvata, Vishvavasu, Haha and Huhu;
Tumburu, Chitrasena, and the renowned messenger of the gods; the great-fortuned maidens of the gods and the divine hosts of apsarases;
Shatadru, Vipasha, Chandrabhaga, Sarasvati, Sindhu, Devika, and the Pushkara tirtha;
Ganga, the great river, Kapila, Narmada, Kampuna, Vishalya, and the Karatoya carrying water;
Sarayu, Gandaki, the great river Lauhitya, Tamraruna, Vetravati, Parnasha, and Gautami;
Godavari, Venna, Krishnaveena, Adrija, Drishadvati, Kaveri, Vankshu and Mandakini;
Prayaga, Prabhasa, the holy Naimisha, and the abode of the lord of the universe, where the clear lake is;
Kurukshetra, crowded with holy tirthas, is celebrated; the best of Sindhu, austerity, gift, and the Jambu road;
the Hiranvati, Vitasta and likewise the Ikshumati river, the Veda-smriti, the Vaidasini, and the Malavasa river;
the holy tracts of land, Gangadvara, the sages' channels, the pure river Chitrapatha;
Kaushiki, Yamuna, Sita, the river Charmanvati, the river Bhimarathi and the great river Bahuda, Mahendravani, Tridiva, Nilika and Sarasvati;
Nanda and Aparananda, the tirtha of the great lake, Gaya, the Phalgu tirtha, and Dharmaranya surrounded by gods;
the holy divine river and the lake made by Brahma, holy, famed in the three worlds, remover of all sins and auspicious;
the mountain Himavan with divine herbs, the Vindhya with its varied mineral limbs, with tirthas and herbs;
Meru, Mahendra, Malaya, Shveta adorned with silver, Shringavan, Mandara, Nila, Nishadha and Dardura;
Chitrakuta, Anjanabha, the mountain Gandhamadana, the holy Somagiri, and other mountains; the directions and intermediate directions, the earth, and all trees:
the Vishvedevas, the sky, the stars and planets: may the gods, named and unnamed by me, protect you always.
A man who recites these is freed from all sins; praising and rejoicing in them, he is freed from every fear and from all mixtures and sins, a delighter in praising the gods.
Next I shall recite the brahmins, perfected by austerity and exceeding in austerity, who free from all sins when recited.
Yavakrita, Raibhya, Kakshivan, Aushija, Bhrigu, Angiras, Kanva, Medhatithi the lord, and Barhi of good qualities took refuge in the eastern direction.
In the auspicious quarter, the greatly fortunate Ulmuchu, Pramuchu, the greatly fortunate Mumuchu, Svasti and the valiant Atreya;
the son of Mitra and Varuna, the mighty Agastya, Dridhayu and Urdhvabahu: these two famed best of sages.
Learn those who prosper in the western direction: Ushadgu with his brothers, and the valiant Paridhyaya;
the sage Dirghatamas, Gautama, Kashyapa, Ekata, Dvita and Trita, the great sages, the righteous son of Atri, and the lord Sarasvata.
Learn those who prosper in the northern direction: Atri, Vasishtha, Shakti, and the valiant Parashara's son;
Vishvamitra, Bharadvaja, Jamadagni, Rama grandson of Richika, and the sage Auddalaki;
Shvetaketu, Kohala, Vipula, Devala, Devasharma, Dhaumya, and Hastikashyapa;
Lomasha, Nachiketas, Lomaharshana, the sage Ugrashravas, Bhargava and Chyavana.
This is the assembly of sages and gods, O king, first recited, which frees from all sins.
Nriga, Yayati, Nahusha, Yadu, the valiant Puru, Dhundhumara, Dilipa, and the mighty Sagara;
Krishashva, Yauvanashva, Chitrashva, Satyavan, Dushyanta, and Bharata the great-famed universal emperor;
Yavana, Janaka, King Dridharatha, Raghu the best of men, and King Dasharatha;
Rama the hero, slayer of rakshasas, Shashabindu, Bhagiratha, Harishchandra, Marutta, and Jahnu served by Jahnavi;
Mahodaya, Alarka, the king Aila, Karandhama best of men, and the king Kadhmora;
Daksha, Ambarisha, Kukura, the greatly renowned Raivata, the royal sage Muchukunda, and Mitra, Bhanu, Priyankara;
Trasadasyu, the royal sage Shveta best of royal sages, the famed Mahabhisha, King Nimi and Ashtaka;
the royal sage Ayu, Kshupa, King Kaksheyu, Shibi Aushinara, and King Gaya;
Pratardana, Divodasa, Saudasa lord of Kosala, Aila, the royal sage Nala, and Manu Prajapati;
Havidhra, Prishadhra, Pratipa, Shantanu, the royal sage Kakshasena, and others not named.
May there be no obstacle, nor sin for me, nor opponents for me; may I have constant victory, and in the next world the highest goal.
[Vaishampayana] O king, Yudhishthira, king of the Kurus, restored to his nature, with all his brothers and the kings who follow him,
attends you, tiger among men, with the wise Krishna. You should give him leave to go to the city.
Thus addressed by the blessed Vyasa, the lord of the earth, the river's son, gave Yudhishthira and his ministers leave.
Then Shantanu's son the king said sweetly: "Enter the city, O king; let the fever of your mind leave you.
Sacrifice with many kinds of sacrifices rich in food and with fees well given, like Yayati, O king, with faith and self-control first.
Devoted to kshatriya dharma, Partha, gratify the ancestors and gods; you will be joined with the good, and let the fever of your mind leave.
Please all subjects, console the people, and honour friends with fruits and honours as is fit.
Dear child, may friends and well-wishers live after you, as birds live on a fruit-bearing tree standing at a shrine."
Saying "So be it," the son of Kunti greeted the Grandsire and went with his retinue to the city of Nagasahvaya.
With Dhritarashtra and the devoted wife Gandhari before him, with all those sages, his brothers and Keshava,
with the townsmen and country people and aged ministers, the king, best of the Kurus, entered the city of Varanasahvaya.
The king, Pandu's son, consoled the women whose heroes and lords had been slain, with great gifts of chariots.
Consecrated, the greatly wise Yudhishthira, having gained the kingdom, then set all his subjects in order.
Receiving the chief blessings from the twice-born, the military chiefs and the townsmen, the best of those who uphold dharma,
after dwelling fifty nights in the best of cities, the glorious best of men remembered the time fixed by the foremost of the Kurus.
He set out from Gajapura, surrounded by priests, having seen the sun turned back and begun its northern course.
Yudhishthira had ghee, garlands, perfumes, silks, sandal and chief aloes, and black aloes sent ahead,
the son of Kunti, to prepare for Bhishma, with very costly garlands and many jewels.
Placing Dhritarashtra before him, and the illustrious Gandhari, and his mother Pritha, the wise best of men with his brothers,
went out of that city like the lord of the gods, and then reached the king, Shantanu's son, at Kurukshetra.
He was attended by the wise Vyasa, Parashara's son, and by Narada, royal sage, and by Devala and Asita,
and by the surviving kings from many lands, the great soul being guarded on all sides by guards.
The king then saw him lying on the hero's bed; then Dharmaraja, with his brothers, descended from the chariot.
Having greeted the Grandsire, scourge of foes, and Dvaipayana and the other brahmins, he was welcomed by them.
With priests like Brahma and with his brothers and Achyuta, he approached the one lying on the bed of arrows, surrounded by sages.
Dharmaraja Yudhishthira, with his brothers, said to the best of the Bharatas, the river's son lying there:

I am Yudhishthira, O king; salutations to you, son of Jahnavi. If you hear, mighty-armed one, tell me what I should do for you.
mahabharata:13:153.20	I have come at the time, O king, having taken the fires, lord; teachers, brahmins, priests and my brothers,
mahabharata:13:153.21	and your son of great radiance, Dhritarashtra the lord of men, are present with their ministers, and the valiant Vasudeva.
mahabharata:13:153.22	The surviving kings and all the people of Kuru-Jangala: look at them, tiger of the Kurus; open your eyes.
mahabharata:13:153.23	Whatever was to be done here, I have done it all; and all was done in time as you said.
So addressed by the wise son of Kunti, Ganga's son saw all the Bharatas standing around him.
Then Bhishma, taking his vast arm with a trembling grip, spoke at the right time with a voice like a flood-cloud.

By good fortune you have come, son of Kunti Yudhishthira, with your ministers; the blessed thousand-rayed sun has turned.
mahabharata:13:153.27	Fifty-eight nights have passed for me lying on sharp-pointed arrows, and they have seemed like a hundred years.
mahabharata:13:153.28	This holy month of Magha has come, Yudhishthira; this bright fortnight with a third remaining should be it.
Having said this to the son of Dharma, Yudhishthira, Ganga's son then addressed Dhritarashtra and spoke at the right time:

O king, you know dharma, with questions decided and doubts removed; you have attended many learned brahmins.
mahabharata:13:153.31	You know all the Vedas and scriptures, and dharmas, O lord of men, and you understand the four Vedas with their limbs in full.
mahabharata:13:153.32	You should not grieve, O Kaurava, for it had to be so. You heard the divine secret even from Krishna Dvaipayana.
mahabharata:13:153.33	As Pandu's sons are yours, O king, by dharma, so protect them, standing in dharma, intent on serving their elders.
mahabharata:13:153.34	The king of dharma, pure in soul, will stay under your command; I know him, devoted to elders, with compassion supreme.
mahabharata:13:153.35	Your sons were evil-souled, given to anger and greed, overcome by envy and of bad conduct; you should not grieve for them.
[Vaishampayana] Having said so much to the wise Dhritarashtra, the Kaurava addressed the mighty-armed Vasudeva.

Blessed one, lord of the gods, saluted by gods and asuras, Trivikrama, salutations to you, bearer of conch, discus and mace.
mahabharata:13:153.38	Give me leave, Krishna, Vaikuntha, Supreme Person; the sons of Pandu are to be protected by you, for you are their refuge.
mahabharata:13:153.39	I told the ill-minded fool Duryodhana long ago: 'Where Krishna is, there is dharma; where dharma is, there is victory.'
mahabharata:13:153.40	'Make peace, son, with the Pandavas through Vasudeva as intermediary; the best time for a treaty is now,' I said again and again.
mahabharata:13:153.41	But that fool of dull mind did not do my word, and having had the earth slaughtered here, he met his end.
mahabharata:13:153.42	And I know you, hero, the ancient best of sages, the god who lived long at Badari with Nara.
mahabharata:13:153.43	So too Narada told me, and Vyasa of great austerity: that these two, Nara and Narayana, were born among men.
[Vasudeva] "I give you leave, Bhishma; attain the Vasus, O king. I have seen no blemish in you, greatly radiant one.
You are devoted to your father, royal sage, like another Markandeya; therefore death stands in your power, bowing like a servant."
[Vaishampayana] So addressed, Ganga's son said this to the Pandavas, and to all with Dhritarashtra at their head and their friends:

I wish to give up my life; you should give me leave. You should strive for truth, for truth is the highest strength.
mahabharata:13:153.48	You should always be compassionate, self-controlled, devoted to brahmins, righteous, and given to austerity and policy, O Bharata.
Having said this and embraced all his friends, the wise one spoke again these words to Yudhishthira:
Brahmins, and especially the wise, teachers and priests, are always to be honoured, O king.
He held himself up by the concentrations in due order, and his life-breaths, stopped, rose upward.
This was a marvel among those great souls: whichever part of his body that Shantanu's son released, that part became free of arrows, as he was joined in yoga.
In an instant, as they watched, he became free of arrows. Seeing it, all were amazed, with Vasudeva at the head, along with all those sages and Vyasa and the rest, O king.
His self, held in all the seats of the body, burst through the crown of the head and flew up to heaven.
A great meteor, O lord of men, issued from Bhishma's crown, entered the sky, and in an instant vanished.
Thus, O tiger among kings, the king, Shantanu's son, the upholder of the Bharata line, was joined with his own worlds.
Then the Pandavas and Vidura, great souls, took logs and many perfumes and made the pyre; Yuyutsu the Kaurava also, and the others were spectators.
Yudhishthira and the greatly wise Vidura both covered Ganga's son, the Kaurava, with silks and garlands.
Then with sandal logs, Kaleyaka wood, black aloes and other perfumes, high and low,
they covered Ganga's son and lit the fire, and the kings with Dhritarashtra at their head circled him keeping him to the left.
Having cremated the best of the Kurus, Ganga's son, the foremost Kurus went to the bank of Bhagirathi, frequented by sages.
Followed by Vyasa, Narada and Asita, Krishna, the women, and the townspeople who had come together,
the best of kshatriyas and all the people offered water for the great-souled son of Ganga, by rule.
Then, when the water-offering for her son was done, the goddess Bhagirathi rose from the water, weeping and lost in sorrow.
Lamenting there, she spoke to the Kauravas: "Hear, blameless ones, what I say as it happened.
Endowed with kingly conduct, wisdom and noble birth, honouring the elders of the Kurus, devoted to his father, firm in vows,
he who was never conquered by Rama, son of Jamadagni, with his divine weapons, he of great valour, was today slain by Shikhandin.
Surely, kings, my heart is made of stone, since it does not burst today as I do not see my dear son.
He who, at the svayamvara in Kashi, defeated with a single chariot the assembled royal kshatriya host and carried off those maidens,
who had no equal on earth in strength, hearing that he was slain by Shikhandin, my heart does not burst.
He who was not much troubled in battle at Kurukshetra by the great-souled Jamadagni's son, was killed by Shikhandin."
As the great river thus lamented much, the lord Damodara consoled her gently.

Be comforted, good one; do not grieve, fair-looking lady. Your son has reached the supreme perfection, without doubt.
mahabharata:13:154.28	This radiant Vasu, fortunate one, because of a curse's fault attained human state; you should not mourn him.
mahabharata:13:154.29	Fighting on the battlefield by kshatriya dharma, he was killed by Dhananjaya; he was not struck down by Shikhandin.
mahabharata:13:154.30	Bhishma, the tiger of the Kurus, with his arrow raised in the great battle, even Shatakratu himself could not have killed him in combat.
mahabharata:13:154.31	Your son went to heaven at his own will, fair-faced one; all the gods could not have killed him in battle.
mahabharata:13:154.32	Therefore, best of rivers, do not mourn the delight of the Kurus; your son has gone to the Vasus, goddess; be free of fever.
So addressed by Krishna and Vyasa, the best of rivers gave up sorrow, great king, and went down into her own water.
Having honoured that river, the kings with Krishna at their head, given leave by her, all turned back, lords of men.
[Marutta] After telling me of you, the best of divine sages gave me leave and entered the fire.
Hearing this from the king, Samvarta, in great joy, said, "I too shall do this much for him."
Then the brahmin, O king, again and again, as if rebuking Marutta with harsh words, said:

I am swayed by the wind, under my own mind's control, of distorted form; how can you wish to have me sacrifice for you?
mahabharata:14:7.9	My brother is able and honoured by Vasava, and is engaged in officiating; have him perform your rites.
mahabharata:14:7.10	My house, my sacrificers, and all the secret deities were taken by my elder brother; only this body is left to me.
mahabharata:14:7.11	Without his leave, son of Avikshit, I could never officiate for you, for he is most to be honoured by me.
mahabharata:14:7.12	Go to Brihaspati and return having got his leave; then I shall officiate for you, if you wish to sacrifice here.
[Marutta] "Hear, Samvarta: I went to Brihaspati before. He does not wish to have me as sacrificer, held back by Vasava.
Having obtained an immortal sacrificer, he said, 'Do not, sage, officiate for Marutta, a mortal, subject to mortal law and afflicted.'
Brahmin, that king always competes with me; and your brother, slayer of Bala and Vritra, said 'So be it.'
When I approached him with love, he did not wish to treat me as a sacrificer; know that he has taken refuge with the king of the gods, best of sages.
So I wish you to officiate for me, even at the cost of all I have; I long to surpass Vasava by the merits you create.
My mind does not incline to go to Brihaspati, brahmin, for I was refused by him though I had done no wrong."
[Samvarta] "You will do as you wish; all that is certain with you, king, if you will do all my intentions.
Brihaspati and Purandara will both be enraged at my officiating for you; accept this one thing.
How will you keep steady in this? Make it free of doubt; angered, I would reduce you to ashes now, with your kin."
[Marutta] "As long as the thousand-rayed sun shines and the mountains stand, so long may I not gain the worlds if I break our agreement.
Nor may I ever gain good understanding here, if I break the agreement in right knowledge or object."
[Samvarta] "Avikshit's son, let a good mind be set on your rites; officiating is also my wish toward you, O king.
I shall provide you, king, supreme imperishable wealth, by which you will overcome the gods, gandharvas and Shakra.
My mind does not turn to wealth or to sacrificers; but I wish to do a disservice to my brother and to Indra, both.
I shall bring you to equality with Indra, certainly; and I shall do what you like. I tell you this truth."
On the roots of trees, in the peaks and cavities and caves of the king of mountains, at will and at ease,
where the blessed Maheshvara always lives with Uma as companion, the radiant trident-bearer, surrounded by various hosts of spirits,
there Rudras, Sadhyas, Vishvedevas, Vasus, Yama, Varuna, and Kubera with his followers,
spirits, pishachas, the two Ashvins, gandharvas, apsarases, yakshas and divine sages,
Adityas, Maruts, and all the yatudhanas attend the great soul, Uma's lord of many forms.
The blessed one delights there with Kubera's followers, deformed and of deformed shapes, sporting, O lord of the earth; he is seen blazing with glory, bright as the morning sun.
His form or shape is not seen at all, and cannot be described by any ordinary creatures with fleshly eyes.
There is neither heat nor cold, nor wind nor sun, nor old age, hunger or thirst, nor death, nor fear, O king.
Having saluted that blessed one: to Sharva, the Ordainer, Rudra, the blue-throated, the fair of form, the radiant,
the matted-haired, the terrible, the tawny-eyed, the boon-giver, the three-eyed, the destroyer of Pushan's teeth, the dwarf, the auspicious,
the Lord of Yama, of unmanifest hair, of good conduct, Shankara, the safe, of green eyes, Sthanu, the Person,
of green hair, the shaven, the lean, the rescuer, the sun-like, of good tirtha, the god of gods, the swift,
the turbaned, of fair face, thousand-eyed, the showerer, the mountain-dweller, the tranquil, the ascetic, wearing bark,
bearing the bilva staff, the perfected, bearing every staff, the deer-hunter, the great, the archer, Bhava,
the excellent, gentle-faced, with animals in hand, the rainer, golden-armed, O king, fierce, lord of the directions,
lord of animals, lord of beings, the Bull, devoted to mothers, the general, the middle one,
with ladle in hand, the lord, the archer, Bhargava, the unborn, the black-eyed, the ill-eyed,
of sharp fangs, the sharp, with fire in his mouth, of great radiance, the bodiless, all-limbed, the possessor of offspring,
and lord of Shukra, the broad, clad in hide, wearing a garland of skulls, always with a golden crown,
to Mahadeva, the dark, the three-eyed, the sinless, the wrathful, the cruel, the gentle, the broad-armed,
the staff-bearing, of heated austerity, the cruel-acting, thousand-headed and thousand-footed; salutations, to svadha in form, of many forms, the tusked.
The Pinaka-bearer, Mahadeva, the great yogi, imperishable, trident in hand, boon-giver, Tryambaka, lord of the world,
slayer of Tripura, three-eyed, lord of the three worlds, of great might, origin of all beings, upholder, bearer of the earth,
Ishana, Shankara, All, Shiva, Lord of the universe, Bhava, Uma's lord, lord of animals, universal form, Maheshvara,
Virupaksha, ten-armed, bearing the bull banner of the Tishya, fierce, Sthanu, Shiva, terrible, Sharva, Gauri's lord of peace,
the blue-throated, the unborn, the white, the broad, the removing, Hara, universal form, ill-eyed, of many forms, Uma's lord:
bowing your head to the god, Hara who removed the limbs of the bodiless, go to Mahadeva, the four-faced refuge, for refuge.
Having thus saluted that swift Mahadeva, great soul, lord of the earth, you will gain that gold. Let your men go there to bring gold.
[Vaishampayana] So addressed, the son of Karandhama did his word; and he made all the arrangements for the sacrifice superhuman, and craftsmen made golden vessels there.
Hearing of King Marutta's prosperity from the gods, Brihaspati was greatly tormented.
Tormented, he became pale and very lean, thinking, "Samvarta will become my enemy, rich in wealth."
Hearing that he was greatly tormented, the king of the gods, surrounded by the immortals, went to Brihaspati and spoke these words.
[Brihaspati] "I sleep happily in my bed, Mahendra, and my servants are agreeable; I wish the gods well, Shakra, and the gods protect me greatly."
[Indra] "Whence your sorrow, of mind or body? Why are you pale and discoloured today? Tell me that, brahmin, and I shall slay all who cause you sorrow."
[Brihaspati] "They say Marutta, Maghavan, is about to sacrifice with a great sacrifice with the best fees; I have heard that Samvarta will officiate for him, and I wish he would not officiate."
[Indra] "All your desires are granted, brahmin, you who counsel the gods as their priest. Both birth and death have passed from you; what can Samvarta do to you today, brahmin?"
[Brihaspati] "With the gods you drive off asuras and wish to kill them with their kin even today; whomever you see prosperous, there is sorrow among rivals when they are prosperous.
Therefore, lord of the gods, I am of altered colour; my rival grows. Hearing that, Maghavan, restrain by all means either Samvarta or King Marutta."
[Indra] "Go, Jatavedas, sent, to hand Brihaspati over to Marutta: say, 'This Brihaspati will officiate for you and make you immortal.'"
[Agni] "I go, Shakra, as your messenger today, to hand Brihaspati over to Marutta, wishing to make Purukutsa's word true and to honour Brihaspati."
The dharma-knowing, high-minded Gandhari, together with Kunti, was served and honoured with attendance by her daughters-in-law, and ate, O Bharata.
The great calamity of the Vrishnis should be told to him. Hearing of the Yadus' misfortune, the greatly radiant lord will come here quickly; I have no doubt of it.
The blessed god Ananta entered Rasatala, at the command of the Grandsire, he who by yoga bore the earth.
